english_translation: All things that are after God have an efficient, exemplary, and final cause. All things are from him, through him, and to him. If, therefore, we consider things as they are constituted by God as efficient cause, they are called beings, because they participate being from God as efficient cause.
exegesis: Pico establishes the metaphysical framework for understanding creation through the Pauline formula 'from him, through him, and to him' (Romans 11:36), integrated with the three Aristotelian causes: efficient, exemplary, and final. All creatures—material bodies, human souls, and angels—receive their being from God as efficient cause and participate in being proportionally to their proximity to God. Angels, as pure intellects requiring no matter or sensory mediation, participate in being most directly and completely. This passage grounds the entire hierarchy of being in an act of divine causality: each level of the hierarchy exists as a degree of participation in divine being received through God's efficient causality, exemplified in divine ideas, and ordered toward divine goodness as final cause.
metaphysical_theme: Creation as participation in divine being through efficient causality; angels as pure intellects participate in being most directly, exemplifying the metaphysical hierarchy through their proximity to divine simplicity

notes: HARVESTER passage U.3.1 provides the systematic metaphysical framework for angelology. The three causes (efficient, exemplary, final) organize Pico's treatment of angels throughout his corpus: angels are beings by participation (efficient), ordered to divine ideas (exemplary), and directed toward divine goodness (final). This passage is foundational to understanding how Pico reconciles Aristotelian and Neoplatonic metaphysics through the doctrine of participation.
